en: The Narra, the Philippine national tree, drops its fragrant yellow flowers in clusters during the dry season.
The Ifugao people built stone-walled rice terraces that use a traditional forest-based irrigation system called muyong.
Filipino scientist Ramon Barba discovered that spraying potassium nitrate makes local mango trees bloom with fruit.
During the Lucban Pahiyas festival, locals decorate their houses with colorful kiping made from ground rice.
The Tboli people of South Cotabato weave tnalak cloth using fibers extracted from the local abaca plant.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, has a distinctive crest of dark brown feathers on its head.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a unique geological formation featuring a volcano inside a lake inside an island.
Filipino citizens fulfill their civic duty to protect the environment by planting mangroves that block coastal storm surges.
The sampaguita, the national flower, is a white jasmine with a strong sweet scent that blooms at night.
The Davao Kadayawan festival features a vibrant street parade displaying locally harvested durian, pomelo, and bananas.
The Badjao people build their traditional seahouse homes on wooden stilts directly over the clear Sulu Sea.
Filipino botanist Leon Maria Guerrero studied and classified native Philippine medicinal plants like the yerba buena mint.
